evals.prompt: Our pricing page test: A had 12,000 visitors and 360 signups, B had 12,100 and 401. We stopped after 4 days because B was winning. Ship B?
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/ab_test.py, reports the lift with CI and p, and flags that 4 days is less than a full week and that stopping when it looked good inflates false positives; recommends keeping it running or rerunning rather than shipping.
expectations: Uses scripts/ab_test.py or reports the CI and p-value
Flags the short duration and early stopping
Does not give an unqualified SHIP

evals.prompt: Test came back p=0.28. So the new onboarding has no effect, right? Control 8,000/1,120 activated, variant 8,050/1,175.
evals.expected_output: Explains the result is inconclusive rather than 'no effect', reports the interval (which includes meaningful positive values), and gives the sample size needed to detect the observed effect.
expectations: States the sample size needed for the observed effect

evals.prompt: We ran 5 headline variants against control. Variant D had p=0.03. Winner?
evals.expected_output: Applies a multiple-comparison correction (e.g. Bonferroni to 0.01 per comparison), concludes D is not significant after correction, and suggests a confirmatory test of D vs control.
expectations: Concludes D is not significant after correction
